newsitem.title: UK: Lead declines overdone, seen higher again - Wolff.
newsitem.headline: Lead declines overdone, seen higher again - Wolff.

text.p: The downside in lead prices has been overdone, and with demand seen strong this year and stocks low the market is forecast to move higher, London Metal Exchange (LME) trader Rudolf Wolff said.

In a special report, Wolff said lead prices have been depressed by fund selling, slow battery manufacturer demand and a general de-stocking. Also, total commercial stocks are very low, and well below critical levels.
However, production stoppages at a number of mines will reduce concentrate availability, limiting China's potential to toll-smelt and export refined metal to the West, Wolff said.

But with demand likely to be strong this year, there is the potential for the lead industry to re-stock. Also, investment funds are believed to be short, so there is short-covering that needs to be done.
"Lower stocks should then underpin prices. We expect a return to $730 in the medium term, but look for a rechallenge of $750/800 later in 1997," Wolff said.
